name: _reshape_alias_copy
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): `aten::_reshape_alias_copy(Tensor self, SymInt[] size, SymInt[] stride) -> Tensor`. All supplied registered schemas, verbatim: `aten::_reshape_alias_copy(Tensor self, SymInt[] size, SymInt[] stride) -> Tensor`; `aten::_reshape_alias_copy.out(Tensor self, SymInt[] size, SymInt[] stride, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!)`. The representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract, including the `out` overload (keyword-only `out`, mutation of `out`, return of that same buffer with unchanged data pointer, shape, strides and storage offset), the positional `self`/`size`/`stride` calling forms, the single Tensor return and the out-alias return, input immutability, and the error cases (rank mismatch between `size` and `stride`, non-tensor input, non-integer stride, and `out` dtype mismatch); do not narrow, delete or rewrite tests to fit this one signature. Semantics: this is the materialising sibling of `_reshape_alias`; it reads `self` through the requested `size`/`stride` view (exercised with permuted and reshaped requests, zero-stride repeats, overlapping reads, and sliced or offset inputs) and returns a fresh tensor of shape `size`, distinct from `self` and not sharing its storage, holding the values read through that view, with the same strides as the ATen reference copy and storage_offset 0; the pytest checks output strides against the reference result rather than asserting a contiguous layout, so no specific output stride pattern is established beyond matching the reference. Layout data (e.g. lazy conjugate bits) is copied as data, not carried on the result. The `out` overload instead fills the caller-supplied buffer, preserves that buffer's shape/stride/offset/pointer, and returns it.
